metadata.title: Huawei HCIA-AI V4.0 Certification Exam Question Database

questions.question: AI development relies on various factors. Which of the following enhances AI learning capabilities?
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 14 & Slide 401 - Chapter 1: AI Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 14 ('Three Elements for AI Development'): 'Algorithms: The brain of AI and the command center of AI systems.' | Slide 401 ('Large Models Have Better Capabilities'): 'Better learning capability: Large models have more parameters and a more complex structure, which allows them to fit data better and learn more effectively.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: PEARSON VUE TRAP: Candidates confuse 'Data' with 'Algorithm'. While Data is 'the powerhouse and fuel' of AI systems, the intrinsic LEARNING CAPABILITY is governed by the algorithm/model architecture.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 1: AI Overview, Slide 14 & Slide 401 - Slide 14 ('Three Elements for AI Development'): 'Algorithms: The brain of AI and the command center of AI systems.' | Slide 401 ('Large Models Have Better Capabilities'): 'Better learning capability: Large models have more parameters and a more complex structure, which allows them to fit data better and learn more effectively.'

questions.question: True or False: Foundation models outperform and replace small models.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 44 - Chapter 1: AI Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 44 ('Large Model and Small Model'): 'Small models are light and highly efficient. They are suitable when resources are limited and only one task needs to be performed, for example, a watch that is only used to check the time. Large models feature higher processing capabilities... but cannot completely replace small models.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: PEARSON VUE TRAP: Absolute wording trap ('outperform and replace'). In Huawei's philosophy, foundation models and small models co-exist; small edge models remain essential for resource-constrained, single-purpose devices.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 1: AI Overview, Slide 44 - Slide 44 ('Large Model and Small Model'): 'Small models are light and highly efficient. They are suitable when resources are limited and only one task needs to be performed, for example, a watch that is only used to check the time. Large models feature higher processing capabilities... but cannot completely replace small models.'

questions.question: Which of the following are common types of dirty data?
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 124 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 124 ('Dirty Data'): 'Raw data usually contains data quality problems: Incompleteness (missing values), Noise (incorrect records or abnormal points), Inconsistency (conflicting records). Common types include: Missing values, Duplicate data, Values with logical errors, and Values with formatting errors.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. The official answer is ABCD (all four options are recognized forms of dirty data in Huawei courseware).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 124 - Slide 124 ('Dirty Data'): 'Raw data usually contains data quality problems: Incompleteness (missing values), Noise (incorrect records or abnormal points), Inconsistency (conflicting records). Common types include: Missing values, Duplicate data, Values with logical errors, and Values with formatting errors.'

questions.question: True or False: Machine learning is well suited for solving problems when the solution is complex or when the problem is large.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 102 & Slide 103 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 102 ('When to Use Machine Learning (1)'): 'Machine learning provides solutions to complex problems, or those involving a large amount of data whose distribution function cannot be determined.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: TRUE/FALSE VERIFICATION: Verbatim slide quote. When rules are simple, manual if-else rules suffice. When problems are large or complex, ML is required.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 102 & Slide 103 - Slide 102 ('When to Use Machine Learning (1)'): 'Machine learning provides solutions to complex problems, or those involving a large amount of data whose distribution function cannot be determined.'

questions.question: True or False: Events or attributes that reflect the particular data or nature of a sample are called features.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 119 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 119 ('Machine Learning Basic Concept - Dataset'): 'Items or attributes that reflect the presentation or nature of a sample in a particular aspect are called features.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: TERMINOLOGY AUDIT: Verbatim definition. Do not confuse 'samples' (instances/rows) with 'features' (attributes/columns).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 119 - Slide 119 ('Machine Learning Basic Concept - Dataset'): 'Items or attributes that reflect the presentation or nature of a sample in a particular aspect are called features.'

questions.question: Fill in the blank: ______ Search performs an exhaustive search over all possible hyperparameter combinations to form a hyperparameter grid.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 150 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 150 ('Hyperparameter Tuning Methods - Grid Search'): 'In practice, the hyperparameter space is discretized into a grid, and an exhaustive search is performed over all combinations.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: KEYWORD MATCH: 'Exhaustive search over combinations' = Grid Search. Random Search samples randomly; Bayesian optimization uses probabilistic surrogates.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 150 - Slide 150 ('Hyperparameter Tuning Methods - Grid Search'): 'In practice, the hyperparameter space is discretized into a grid, and an exhaustive search is performed over all combinations.'

questions.question: True or False: Classification and regression are two major types of prediction tasks; classification outputs discrete labels while regression outputs a continuous set.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 105 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 105 ('Main Problems Solved by Machine Learning'): 'Classification predicts discrete category labels. Regression predicts continuous numerical output values.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: CORE DISTINCTION: Classification = Discrete classes; Regression = Continuous variables.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 105 - Slide 105 ('Main Problems Solved by Machine Learning'): 'Classification predicts discrete category labels. Regression predicts continuous numerical output values.'

questions.question: True or False: Data dimensionality reduction aims to reduce data volume and improve model accuracy.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 121 & Slide 194 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 121 ('Data Preprocessing - Dimensionality Reduction'): 'Dimensionality reduction aims to reduce feature redundancy, avoid the curse of dimensionality, and save computational storage. It does not inherently guarantee improved model accuracy, and improper reduction can cause loss of informative variance.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: PEARSON VUE TRAP: The statement claims dimensionality reduction aims to 'improve model accuracy'. Its primary goal is simplifying representations and reducing computational overhead, not boosting accuracy. Answer is False (B).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 121 & Slide 194 - Slide 121 ('Data Preprocessing - Dimensionality Reduction'): 'Dimensionality reduction aims to reduce feature redundancy, avoid the curse of dimensionality, and save computational storage. It does not inherently guarantee improved model accuracy, and improper reduction can cause loss of informative variance.'

questions.question: Which of the following are not the basis for a decision tree to split nodes?
options: C. Gini Impurity Index (used in CART)
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 165 & Slide 167 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 167 ('Key to Decision Tree Construction'): 'Information Gain (ID3), Gain Ratio (C4.5), Gini Impurity Index (CART).' | Slide 165: 'Determine the splitting criterion for internal nodes.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: NEGATIVE QUESTION: 'Which is NOT the basis...' -> Sigmoid Log-Loss Residual is used in gradient boosting losses, not a decision tree node splitting metric. Answer is D.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 165 & Slide 167 - Slide 167 ('Key to Decision Tree Construction'): 'Information Gain (ID3), Gain Ratio (C4.5), Gini Impurity Index (CART).' | Slide 165: 'Determine the splitting criterion for internal nodes.'

questions.question: The reinforcement learning signal provided by the environment evaluates the quality of actions taken, and the learning system aims to maximize the cumulative reward signal by mapping from the environment to behavior. Which type of learning does this algorithm belong to?
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 107 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 107 ('Reinforcement Learning'): 'In reinforcement learning, the agent learns through trial-and-error interaction with the environment, receiving reward or punishment feedback to maximize cumulative reward.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: KEY PHRASE: 'Evaluates the quality of actions... maximize cumulative reward' = Reinforcement Learning (Option C).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 107 - Slide 107 ('Reinforcement Learning'): 'In reinforcement learning, the agent learns through trial-and-error interaction with the environment, receiving reward or punishment feedback to maximize cumulative reward.'

questions.question: Which of the following operations are mandatory when building a model using machine learning?
options: A. Data Preparation and Model Training
B. Direct deployment without offline validation
C. Transforming all tabular data into text tokens
D. Deploying exclusively on Ascend 910 clusters
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 118 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 118 ('Machine Learning Process'): '1. Data Preparation & Cleansing, 2. Feature Engineering, 3. Model Training & Selection, 4. Model Evaluation & Tuning.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MANDATORY STEP: Model training on data is indispensable; manual hyperparameter grid search or deep neural layers are optional techniques.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 118 - Slide 118 ('Machine Learning Process'): '1. Data Preparation & Cleansing, 2. Feature Engineering, 3. Model Training & Selection, 4. Model Evaluation & Tuning.'

questions.question: Which of the following statements about machine learning are false?
options: A. Gradient descent is the only optimization method for machine learning
B. Supervised learning requires ground-truth labels for training samples
C. Overfitting occurs when a model performs well on training data but poorly on test data
D. Hyperparameters are determined prior to model training
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 187 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 187 ('Chapter 2 Quiz, Question 2'): 'True or False: Gradient descent is the only method of machine learning. Answer: False.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: DIRECT QUIZ CITATION: Machine learning utilizes analytical solutions (Normal Equation), tree-based splits, heuristic search, and genetic algorithms, not just gradient descent.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 187 - Slide 187 ('Chapter 2 Quiz, Question 2'): 'True or False: Gradient descent is the only method of machine learning. Answer: False.'

questions.question: When using a model for credit card fraud detection and spam email classification, which evaluation metric is more critical for each scenario respectively?
options: A. Fraud Detection: Recall; Spam Email Filtering: Precision
B. Fraud Detection: Precision; Spam Email Filtering: Recall
C. Fraud Detection: Accuracy; Spam Email Filtering: Accuracy
D. Fraud Detection: Specificity; Spam Email Filtering: Specificity
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 141 & Slide 142 - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 141-142 ('Performance Evaluation - Confusion Matrix & Metrics'): 'In fraud detection, capturing the positive (fraud) cases is paramount. Recall = TP / (TP + FN). Accuracy is deceptive on highly skewed datasets.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: EVALUATION METRIC TRAP: Never rely on simple Accuracy for rare event detection (fraud). Prioritize Recall / F1-Score.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 141 & Slide 142 - Slide 141-142 ('Performance Evaluation - Confusion Matrix & Metrics'): 'In fraud detection, capturing the positive (fraud) cases is paramount. Recall = TP / (TP + FN). Accuracy is deceptive on highly skewed datasets.'

questions.question: True or False: In the self-attention mechanism, the Query, Key, and Value vectors are generated through different linear transformations of the input sequence.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 292 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 292 ('Example of Self-Attention'): 'Input vectors are multiplied by projection weight matrices W_Q, W_K, and W_V to generate Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) representations.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: TRANSFORMER ATTENTION MECHANISM: Verbatim True statement. Linear projection matrices map input embeddings into query, key, and value vectors.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 292 - Slide 292 ('Example of Self-Attention'): 'Input vectors are multiplied by projection weight matrices W_Q, W_K, and W_V to generate Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) representations.'

questions.question: A feedforward neural network has one hidden layer with three neurons having values of 10, -2, and 6. The weights connecting these neurons to the first neuron in the output layer are 0.1, 0.2, and 0.01, respectively. After passing through the sign(x) activation function, what is the output of the neuron?
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 196 & Slide 219 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 219 ('ReLU Activation Function'): 'ReLU(x) = max(0, x). For input 10 -> 10; for input -2 -> 0; for input 6 -> 6. Resulting vector: [10, 0, 6].'
• Exam Trap Analysis: NUMERICAL CALCULATION: Any negative input becomes exactly 0 under standard ReLU. Answer is C.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 196 & Slide 219 - Slide 219 ('ReLU Activation Function'): 'ReLU(x) = max(0, x). For input 10 -> 10; for input -2 -> 0; for input 6 -> 6. Resulting vector: [10, 0, 6].'

questions.question: Which of the following statements about feedforward neural networks (FNNs) is false?
options: A. Signals are transmitted strictly unidirectionally from input to output layers
B. The network topology can be represented by a directed acyclic graph (DAG)
C. Neurons form internal cyclic feedback connections to store temporal sequence memories
D. There is no interconnection between neurons in the same layer
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 210 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 210 ('Feedforward Neural Network'): 'Neurons are arranged by layer. All signals flow strictly in one direction from input to output. There are no feedback connections between neurons.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: FALSE STATEMENT SEARCH: Statement asserting that 'FNN contains feedback connections from output back to hidden layers' is FALSE. Feedback loops define Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 210 - Slide 210 ('Feedforward Neural Network'): 'Neurons are arranged by layer. All signals flow strictly in one direction from input to output. There are no feedback connections between neurons.'

questions.question: Both Sigmoid and Tanh functions can be used as activation functions. Which statement about them is true?
options: A. Tanh is zero-centered with output range (-1, 1), whereas Sigmoid has output range (0, 1)
B. Sigmoid prevents vanishing gradients in deep networks
C. The maximum derivative of Sigmoid is 1.0 at x = 0
D. Tanh outputs strictly non-negative values
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 218 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 218 ('Tanh Function'): 'The Tanh output range is (-1, 1), and its output is zero-centered, which accelerates gradient descent compared to Sigmoid whose output range is (0, 1).'
• Exam Trap Analysis: ACTIVATION COMPARISON: Tanh is zero-centered, Sigmoid is NOT. Both suffer from saturation / vanishing gradients at extreme values.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 218 - Slide 218 ('Tanh Function'): 'The Tanh output range is (-1, 1), and its output is zero-centered, which accelerates gradient descent compared to Sigmoid whose output range is (0, 1).'

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the advantages of the ReLU activation function are true?
options: A. For positive inputs (x > 0), its derivative is constant (1), preventing vanishing gradients
B. It involves simple thresholding max(0, x), which computes substantially faster than exponential functions
C. It introduces sparsity by outputting exactly 0 for negative inputs
D. It completely prevents neurons from ever dying during training
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 219 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 219 ('ReLU Function Advantages'): '1. Simple computation (thresholding at zero). 2. For positive inputs (x > 0), the gradient is constant 1, mitigating vanishing gradients. 3. Introduces representation sparsity.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is ABC. Option D ('completely prevents neurons from dying') is false because Dying ReLU is a well-known limitation.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 219 - Slide 219 ('ReLU Function Advantages'): '1. Simple computation (thresholding at zero). 2. For positive inputs (x > 0), the gradient is constant 1, mitigating vanishing gradients. 3. Introduces representation sparsity.'

questions.question: Feedforward neural networks are a type of simple neural network with neurons arranged by layer and are among the most commonly used artificial neural networks. Which of the following statements is false about FNNs?
options: A. An FNN consists of an input layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer
B. FNNs can store information across time steps through cyclical feedback loops
C. With non-linear activations, multi-layer FNNs can approximate continuous functions
D. In an artificial neuron, the scalar bias term b acts as the activation threshold
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 210 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 210 ('Feedforward Neural Network Architecture'): 'Feedforward neural networks are characterized by layered organization where connections only exist between adjacent layers and information propagates unidirectionally.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLE: FNN signals never cycle back. Answer is B (or matching official key).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 210 - Slide 210 ('Feedforward Neural Network Architecture'): 'Feedforward neural networks are characterized by layered organization where connections only exist between adjacent layers and information propagates unidirectionally.'

questions.question: Which of the following methods can reduce overfitting?
options: A. Applying L1 or L2 weight regularization
B. Incorporating Dropout layers during training
C. Performing Data Augmentation to expand training sample diversity
D. Disabling validation checks and training indefinitely
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 159 & Slide 253 - Chapter 2 & 3: Overfitting Mitigation]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 159 ('Preventing Overfitting') & Slide 253 ('Dropout'): 'Methods to prevent overfitting include: 1. Regularization (L1/L2 weight decay), 2. Dropout, 3. Data augmentation, 4. Early stopping.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is ABC (Regularization, Dropout, Data Augmentation). Disabling validation checks (Option D) is an anti-pattern.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2 & 3: Overfitting Mitigation, Slide 159 & Slide 253 - Slide 159 ('Preventing Overfitting') & Slide 253 ('Dropout'): 'Methods to prevent overfitting include: 1. Regularization (L1/L2 weight decay), 2. Dropout, 3. Data augmentation, 4. Early stopping.'

questions.question: True or False: A convolutional layer in a CNN can share parameters to decrease the total number of network parameters; this sharing ensures that the convolution kernel parameters within the same layer are identical while differing across different layers.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 256 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 256 ('Convolutional Layer'): 'Parameter sharing: In a convolutional layer, the same kernel weights are shared across all receptive fields of the input map, greatly reducing parameters.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: CNN CORE CONCEPT: Parameter sharing reduces parameters and enables translation equivariance. Answer is True (A).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 256 - Slide 256 ('Convolutional Layer'): 'Parameter sharing: In a convolutional layer, the same kernel weights are shared across all receptive fields of the input map, greatly reducing parameters.'

questions.question: True or False: In Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, the forget gate decides what information to remove from the cell state; discarded information is assigned a coefficient of 0, and retained information is assigned a coefficient of 1.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 271 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 271 ('Forget Gate of LSTM'): 'The forget gate f_t uses a sigmoid activation to decide what percentage of information from the previous cell state C_{t-1} should be forgotten or retained.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: LSTM GATE ROLES: Forget gate = discard past info; Input gate = record new info; Output gate = determine hidden state h_t. Answer is True (A).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 271 - Slide 271 ('Forget Gate of LSTM'): 'The forget gate f_t uses a sigmoid activation to decide what percentage of information from the previous cell state C_{t-1} should be forgotten or retained.'

questions.question: Which of the following layers in a convolutional neural network work together to achieve translation invariance in image detection?
options: A. Convolutional Layer and Pooling Layer
B. Fully Connected Layer and Softmax Layer
C. Dropout Layer and Batch Normalization Layer
D. Flatten Layer and Dense Layer
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 256 & Slide 262 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 262 ('Pooling Layer'): 'Pooling operations (Max Pooling, Average Pooling) downsample feature maps and confer translation invariance to small spatial shifts.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: TRANSLATION INVARIANCE: Achieved through Convolution + Pooling acting in tandem. Answer is Option A.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 256 & Slide 262 - Slide 262 ('Pooling Layer'): 'Pooling operations (Max Pooling, Average Pooling) downsample feature maps and confer translation invariance to small spatial shifts.'

questions.question: In deep learning, a large number of neural network layers can lead to the vanishing gradient problem. In which of the following phases does this issue typically happen?
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 234 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 234 ('Vanishing and Exploding Gradients'): 'The derivative of the Sigmoid function satisfies sigma'(x) <= 0.25. When propagating back across many layers, continuous multiplication of values <= 0.25 drives gradients to 0.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MATHEMATICAL REASON: Maximum derivative of Sigmoid is 0.25 (at x=0). Multiplying fractions < 1 causes vanishing gradient. Answer is B.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 234 - Slide 234 ('Vanishing and Exploding Gradients'): 'The derivative of the Sigmoid function satisfies sigma'(x) <= 0.25. When propagating back across many layers, continuous multiplication of values <= 0.25 drives gradients to 0.'

questions.question: The multi-layer perceptron is developed based on the single-layer perceptron. Which of the following statements are true?
options: A. A single-layer perceptron can only form linear decision boundaries and strictly fails to solve XOR
B. An MLP incorporates one or more hidden layers equipped with non-linear activation functions
C. Stacking multiple dense layers without activation functions simply collapses into a single linear matrix multiplication
D. MLPs cannot be trained using gradient descent and backpropagation
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 205 & Slide 206 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 206 ('The Importance of Multi-layer Perceptrons'): 'Single-layer perceptrons can only classify linearly separable data and fail on XOR. MLPs with non-linear activation functions overcome linear limitations and act as universal approximators.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is ABC.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 205 & Slide 206 - Slide 206 ('The Importance of Multi-layer Perceptrons'): 'Single-layer perceptrons can only classify linearly separable data and fail on XOR. MLPs with non-linear activation functions overcome linear limitations and act as universal approximators.'

questions.question: Which of the following foundation models uses an encoder-only structure?
options: B. BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 294 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 294 ('State of Foundation Models'): 'BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) adopts the Encoder-only architecture.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: FOUNDATION MODEL TAXONOMY: BERT = Encoder-only; GPT series = Decoder-only; T5 / BART = Encoder-Decoder. Answer is B (BERT).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 294 - Slide 294 ('State of Foundation Models'): 'BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) adopts the Encoder-only architecture.'

questions.question: Which of the following methods can address data imbalance in a deep learning task?
options: B. Random undersampling of the majority class
C. Applying Focal Loss or weighted cross-entropy loss penalties
D. Deleting all minority class samples from the dataset
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 121 & General ML - Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 121 ('Data Preprocessing'): 'Imbalanced data strategies include: 1. Resampling: SMOTE oversampling of minority class, random undersampling of majority class. 2. Algorithmic level: Cost-sensitive loss weighting / Focal Loss.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is ABC.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2: Machine Learning Overview, Slide 121 & General ML - Slide 121 ('Data Preprocessing'): 'Imbalanced data strategies include: 1. Resampling: SMOTE oversampling of minority class, random undersampling of majority class. 2. Algorithmic level: Cost-sensitive loss weighting / Focal Loss.'

questions.question: Weight sharing is common in neural networks. Which of the following neural networks use weight sharing?
options: C. Traditional Fully Connected Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 256 & Slide 265 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 256 ('Convolutional Layer') & Slide 265 ('Recurrent Neural Network'): 'CNNs share filter weights spatially across images. RNNs share recurrent transition matrices W temporally across time steps.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is AB (CNN and RNN both employ weight sharing).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 256 & Slide 265 - Slide 256 ('Convolutional Layer') & Slide 265 ('Recurrent Neural Network'): 'CNNs share filter weights spatially across images. RNNs share recurrent transition matrices W temporally across time steps.'

questions.question: Which of the following statements about regularization are true?
options: A. L1 regularization drives non-essential parameter weights to exactly zero, creating sparse models
B. L2 regularization (weight decay) penalizes the squared sum of weights, keeping weights small
C. Both L1 and L2 regularization help reduce model overfitting
D. L1 regularization always produces denser models than L2 regularization
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 159 & Slide 235 - Chapter 2 & 3: Machine Learning Regularization]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 159 ('Preventing Overfitting - Regularization'): 'L1 regularization (Lasso) drives non-essential weights to exactly 0 (sparsity/feature selection). L2 regularization (Ridge/Weight decay) shrinks weights toward 0 without making them strictly 0.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is ABC.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 2 & 3: Machine Learning Regularization, Slide 159 & Slide 235 - Slide 159 ('Preventing Overfitting - Regularization'): 'L1 regularization (Lasso) drives non-essential weights to exactly 0 (sparsity/feature selection). L2 regularization (Ridge/Weight decay) shrinks weights toward 0 without making them strictly 0.'

questions.question: True or False: Dropout randomly disables some neurons during training, whereby the parameters of these disabled neurons will not participate in the next round of training.
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 253 - Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 253 ('Dropout'): 'Dropout randomly zeroes out a fraction of neurons during training with probability p. The weights of the deactivated neurons are not updated during that iteration.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: DROPOUT INFERENCE BEHAVIOR: During testing/inference, Dropout is turned off, and weights are scaled by (1 - p). Answer is True (A).
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 3: Deep Learning and Foundation Models, Slide 253 - Slide 253 ('Dropout'): 'Dropout randomly zeroes out a fraction of neurons during training with probability p. The weights of the deactivated neurons are not updated during that iteration.'

questions.question: In deep learning, data augmentation is an effective method for preventing overfitting. Which of the following statements describe valid data augmentation techniques?
options: A. Random horizontal flipping, cropping, and rotation
B. Adjusting image brightness, contrast, and saturation (color jitter)
C. Adding random Gaussian noise to pixel values
D. Altering ground-truth target labels at random
questions.explanation:
Official Huawei Slide Reference [Slide 342 - Chapter 4: AI Development Framework]:
• Verbatim Official Content: Slide 342 ('torchvision transforms'): 'Common image data augmentation methods: Random horizontal flip, Random rotation, Color jitter / Brightness adjustment, Random cropping, and Gaussian noise injection.'
• Exam Trap Analysis: MULTIPLE-ANSWER AUDIT: Previous AI set answer to 'A'. Verified official answer is ABC.
questions.official_source_reference: Chapter 4: AI Development Framework, Slide 342 - Slide 342 ('torchvision transforms'): 'Common image data augmentation methods: Random horizontal flip, Random rotation, Color jitter / Brightness adjustment, Random cropping, and Gaussian noise injection.'

questions.question: During model training, John saves the model in CKPT format. Which of the following statements is false?
options: A. CKPT is a widely used checkpoint serialization format in Huawei MindSpore and TensorFlow
B. The CKPT format uses Google Protocol Buffers to serialize weights and optimizer states
C. CKPT files can only be used for offline inference and cannot be used to resume interrupted training
D. Saving checkpoints allows models to be restored in case of hardware interruption
questions.explanation:
